properties.name: Ur
properties.note: Sumer and Akkad, the heartland the kings of Ur ruled directly; at their height they also held lands to the north and east. Drawn by hand: Cliopatria has no outline for them.

properties.name: Judah
properties.note: The tribes' lands as Joshua 13–19 allots them, roughly; boundaries follow the usual Bible-atlas reading. Much of the coastal plain stayed Philistine (Judges 1:18–19).

properties.name: Simeon
properties.note: Simeon's towns lay within Judah's land, around Beersheba (Joshua 19:1–9).

properties.name: Benjamin
properties.note: The tribes' lands as Joshua 13–19 allots them, roughly; boundaries follow the usual Bible-atlas reading.

properties.name: Dan
properties.note: Dan's first allotment, beside the Philistines (Joshua 19:40–48). Pressed by the Amorites and Philistines, the tribe moved north and took Laish, renaming it Dan (Judges 18).

properties.name: Ephraim
properties.note: The tribes' lands as Joshua 13–19 allots them, roughly; boundaries follow the usual Bible-atlas reading.

properties.name: Manasseh
properties.note: Half the tribe settled west of the Jordan, half in Gilead and Bashan to the east (Joshua 13:29–31; 17).

properties.name: Issachar
properties.note: The tribes' lands as Joshua 13–19 allots them, roughly; boundaries follow the usual Bible-atlas reading.

properties.name: Zebulun
properties.note: The tribes' lands as Joshua 13–19 allots them, roughly; boundaries follow the usual Bible-atlas reading.

properties.name: Asher
properties.note: Asher's allotment reached Sidon (Joshua 19:28), but the tribe never drove out the coastal cities (Judges 1:31).

properties.name: Naphtali
properties.note: The tribes' lands as Joshua 13–19 allots them, roughly; boundaries follow the usual Bible-atlas reading.

properties.name: Gad
properties.note: Gad and Reuben chose the pastures east of the Jordan (Numbers 32; Joshua 13:15–28).

properties.name: Reuben
properties.note: Gad and Reuben chose the pastures east of the Jordan (Numbers 32; Joshua 13:15–28).

properties.name: Israel
properties.note: Saul's kingdom, roughly: the hill country, Gilead and Galilee. The Philistines still held the coastal plain, and their garrisons reached into the hills (1 Samuel 13).

properties.name: Israel
properties.note: Israel under David and Solomon, "from Dan to Beersheba" (1 Kings 4:25), roughly. Gaza, Ashkelon and Ashdod stayed Philistine.

properties.name: Subject to Israel
properties.note: Lands David conquered or made pay tribute, Edom, Moab, Ammon and Aram (2 Samuel 8), which Solomon held "from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines" (1 Kings 4:21). How far his rule really reached is debated.

properties.name: Israel
properties.note: The northern kingdom, roughly. Its borders moved with its wars: Aram took and lost Gilead and Bashan, and under Jeroboam II Israel reached Hamath (2 Kings 14:25).

properties.name: Israel
properties.note: What was left of Israel after Tiglath-pileser took Galilee, Gilead and the coast in 732 BC (2 Kings 15:29), until Samaria fell in 722.

properties.name: Judah
properties.note: The southern kingdom, roughly, from the Benjamin border just north of Jerusalem into the Negev. At times it also held Edom and Elath (2 Kings 14:22); Sennacherib gave towns of the Shephelah to the Philistines after 701 BC.

properties.name: Yehud
properties.note: The small Persian province the exiles returned to, from Mizpah to Beth-zur (Nehemiah 3), roughly.

properties.name: Judea
properties.note: Judea under the Ptolemies and then the Seleucids, much the same land as Persian Yehud, until the Maccabees won it independence.

properties.name: Galilee and Perea
properties.note: Herod Antipas's tetrarchy after his father's death, where Jesus grew up and did most of his work (Luke 3:1), until Caligula exiled him in AD 39.

properties.name: Philip's tetrarchy
properties.note: Ituraea and Trachonitis, east and north of the Sea of Galilee, ruled by Herod's son Philip (Luke 3:1) until his death in AD 34. Caesarea Philippi was his capital.

properties.name: Judea
properties.note: Judea, Samaria and Idumea under Herod's son Archelaus (Matthew 2:22), until Rome removed him in AD 6.

properties.name: Judea
properties.note: Judea, Samaria and Idumea as a Roman province, governed by prefects (Pontius Pilate from AD 26 to 36) from Caesarea.

properties.name: Agrippa's kingdom
properties.note: Herod Agrippa I ruled all his grandfather's kingdom from AD 41 until his death in 44 (Acts 12).

properties.name: Judea
properties.note: After Agrippa I died, Rome governed Judea and Galilee through procurators (Felix, Festus), until the revolts of AD 66 and 132. Rome then renamed the province Syria Palaestina.

properties.name: Ammon
properties.note: Rough: the land around Rabbah (today's Amman), east of Gilead. Its border with Gad moved with every war, from Jephthah's (Judges 11) to David's, who took Rabbah (2 Samuel 12:29). Ammon kept its kings under Assyria and Babylon, as Judah did, until Nebuchadnezzar ended it about 582 BC (Josephus).

properties.name: Moab
properties.note: Rough: from the Arnon to the Zered, east of the Dead Sea (Numbers 21:13). Moab often held the plain north of the Arnon too, as King Mesha did when he rebelled after Ahab's death (2 Kings 3:5). It kept its kings under Assyria and Babylon, as Judah did, until Nebuchadnezzar ended it about 582 BC (Josephus).

properties.name: Edom
properties.note: Rough: the highlands south of the Zered, east of the Arabah. Judah ruled Edom through a deputy (1 Kings 22:47) until it rebelled in Jehoram's day (2 Kings 8:20), though the map draws Edom's land on its own throughout. Edom kept its kings under Assyria and Babylon until Babylon's king Nabonidus ended it about 552 BC; Edomites then moved west into the Negev, later Idumea.

properties.name: Aram
properties.note: Rough: the Aramean kingdom of Damascus. Rezon took Damascus in Solomon's day (1 Kings 11:23–24); its kings, Ben-hadad and Hazael, were Israel's great rivals until Assyria took Damascus in 732 BC (2 Kings 16:9). Its border with Israel in Bashan and Gilead moved with every war.
